Create a docs-only bounded enabler for T2: draft the proposed canonical tenancy model RFC for later review before further tenant-management backend/frontend implementation. Actor: platform operator and downstream backend/frontend workers. Trigger: after TMP-016 partner channel onboarding contracts are archived and before activating tenant-management implementation WorkOrders TMP-048, TMP-051, TMP-055, TMP-057, TMP-065, TMP-071, or TMP-074. Outcome: a proposed RFC document exists at docs/architecture/canonical-tenancy-model.md defining tenant identity, tenant/channel hierarchy, admin membership source of truth, platform-vs-tenant scope, onboarding lifecycle, credential-reference boundaries, resolver precedence, migration/enforcement gates, and downstream WorkOrders that must consume the RFC. The slice does not approve the RFC; completion means draft ready for independent review. Allowed files: docs/architecture/canonical-tenancy-model.md, docs/admin-tenant-account-mapping.md, docs/tenant-channel-onboarding.md, docs/tenant-platform-migration-runbook.md, docs/tenant-nullability-enforcement-plan.md, agent/backlog/issues/TMP-canonical-tenancy-model.md, agent/state/goals/**, agent/state/hvc/**, agent/state/work-orders/ready/**, slices/manifest.json, slices/T2-canonical-tenancy-model/**, .harness/**. Forbidden files: services/**, frontend/**, common/**, scripts/**, ops/**, docker-compose*.yml, go.mod, go.sum, package.json, package-lock.json, **/.env, secrets/**. Acceptance proof: RFC names canonical tenancy entities and ownership boundaries; RFC reconciles the four existing tenant docs as source inputs or superseded fragments; RFC lists downstream WorkOrders blocked on or consuming the decision; no backend, frontend, migration, deployment, dependency, or secret files are changed; schema validate-all and reconcile pass after WorkOrder emission and evidence recording.
Use capsule-first context for dispatched agents.
